topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: Increasing array size in SIW arrays for high-gain inter-satellite antennas enhances radiation efficiency but introduces higher insertion loss, reducing gain by up to 1.5 dB. This trade-off impacts the link budget and capacity. To balance performance and compactness, hybrid feeding topologies, precise material modeling, and advanced simulation tools are essential. Accurate material properties are crucial, as inaccuracies can lead to discrepancies between simulated and measured gains, impacting link budget. Network management should prioritize resource allocation and interference mitigation strategies to maximize capacity under these constraints. By integrating these strategies, one can achieve high gain while minimizing insertion loss and adhering to size and power constraints.
